title: Maximum Subarray
summary: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum. Walk once, keeping the best sum of a subarray ending here: either extend the previous one or start fresh at the current number, whichever is bigger.
intuition: `cur = max(x, cur + x)`: a negative running sum only drags future sums down, so drop it.
Track the best `cur` ever seen.
Initialise with the first element so all-negative arrays work.
pitfalls: Initialising best to 0 returns 0 for all-negative input.
Resetting `cur` to 0 instead of to x.

title: Jump Game
summary: Each value is the maximum jump from that index. Can you reach the end? Track the farthest index reachable so far. If you ever stand on an index beyond it, you're stuck.

complexity.note: Stops as soon as the end is reachable.

intuition: `reach = max(reach, i + nums[i])` for every index you can stand on.
If `i > reach`, index i can't be reached, and neither can anything after it.
No need to know which jumps to take.
pitfalls: BFS or DP over all jumps is O(n²).
Treating a 0 at the last index as a problem; you're already there.

title: Merge Intervals
summary: Merge all overlapping intervals. Sort by start. Walk through them: if an interval starts before the last merged one ends, extend that end; otherwise start a new merged interval.
intuition: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are next to each other.
Only the last merged interval can overlap the current one.
Touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] count as overlapping.
pitfalls: Setting the new end to the current end instead of `max(end, cur.end)` breaks on [1,10], [2,3].
Comparing with `<` instead of `<=` misses touching intervals.

title: Insert Interval
summary: Insert a new interval into a sorted, non-overlapping list and merge as needed. Copy every interval that ends before the new one starts, merge every interval that overlaps it, then copy the rest.

complexity.note: The input is already sorted, so no sort is needed.

intuition: Phase 1: `end < new.start` → entirely before, copy it.
Phase 2: `start <= new.end` → overlaps, grow the new interval.
Phase 3: everything else is after, copy it.
pitfalls: Re-sorting and running Merge Intervals works but is O(n log n).
Forgetting to add the merged new interval itself.

Python.code:
def insert(intervals: List[List[int]], newInterval: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
    res, i, n = [], 0, len(intervals)
    lo, hi = newInterval
    while i < n and intervals[i][1] < lo:
        res.append(intervals[i])
        i += 1
    while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= hi:
        lo = min(lo, intervals[i][0])
        hi = max(hi, intervals[i][1])
        i += 1
    res.append([lo, hi])
    res.extend(intervals[i:])
    return res

title: Jump Game II
summary: Find the fewest jumps to reach the end. Think in levels: all indices reachable with k jumps form a window. While scanning the current window, track the farthest you could get with one more jump; when you reach the window's end, take a jump and move to the next window.
intuition: `end` marks the edge of what the current number of jumps can reach.
`far` is the farthest reachable with one more jump from anywhere in the window.
At `i == end`, you must jump: `jumps++`, `end = far`.
Loop to `n − 2`: you never jump from the last index.
pitfalls: Looping to n − 1 counts an extra jump when `end` lands exactly on the last index.
Greedily jumping as far as possible from each position is wrong.

title: Gas Station
summary: Find the station from which you can drive the whole circle. If total gas ≥ total cost, a solution exists. Drive from station 0 keeping the tank; whenever the tank goes negative, no station from the current start up to here works, so start fresh at the next station.
intuition: If the total gas is less than the total cost, it's impossible from anywhere.
If you run dry at station i starting from s, every start between s and i also runs dry by i.
So jump the start to i + 1 and reset the tank.
pitfalls: Forgetting the total check: the last start candidate isn't guaranteed without it.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Remove the fewest intervals so the rest don't overlap. Sort by end time and greedily keep each interval that starts at or after the last kept end. Keeping the earliest-ending interval leaves the most room for the rest.
intuition: This is activity selection: maximise kept intervals, then removed = n − kept.
Sort by end, not start.
Touching intervals ([1,2] and [2,3]) don't overlap here.
pitfalls: Sorting by start and keeping the first can keep a long interval that blocks many.
Using `>` instead of `>=` treats touching intervals as overlapping.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
summary: Each balloon spans [start, end] on the x-axis; an arrow at x bursts every balloon covering x. Sort by end; shoot at the first balloon's end, which bursts everything starting at or before it. The next balloon that starts after the arrow needs a new arrow.
intuition: Shooting at the smallest end bursts the most balloons that must be burst anyway.
A balloon starting after the arrow's x needs a new arrow.
Touching counts: a balloon starting exactly at x is burst.
pitfalls: `a[1] - b[1]` in the comparator overflows for values near ±2³¹; use Integer.compare.
Using `>=` when comparing start to the arrow, which misses touching balloons.
